URL: https://abcnews.com/International/ukraine-attacks-crimean-bridge-2nd-consecutive-night-officials/story?id=138201512
ABC News, published 19 November 2026

4:34This grab taken from a video released on Nov. 17, 2026 by the Ukrainian Security Service shows damage to the Crimean bridge that links Crimea to Russia, near Kerch.Ukrainian Security Service via AFP via Getty ImagesLONDON -- Ukraine targeted the Crimean bridge for a second consecutive night on Monday, according to Ukrainian officials and Russian-aligned authorities on the occupied Ukrainian peninsula, with Kyiv claiming to have inflicted serious damage on the structure.

"The enemy attacked the Crimean bridge again. Currently, traffic is suspended," Sergey Aksenov, the Moscow-appointed head of occupied Crimea, said in a post to Telegram on Monday night.

On Tuesday morning, Aksenov said that two people were killed in a drone attack in the Lenin district of the peninsula, close to Kerch where the bridge joins Crimea.

Mikhail Razvozhayev, the governor of the city of Sevastopol -- Crimea's largest city -- posted to Telegram urging residents to delay any planned journeys across the bridge. "The Ukrainian Armed Forces have once again attacked the Crimean bridge," he wrote. "Traffic has been suspended."

This grab taken from a video released on Nov. 17, 2026 by the Ukrainian Security Service shows damage to the Crimean bridge that links Crimea to Russia, near Kerch.Ukrainian Security Service via AFP via Getty ImagesRelatedWitkoff and Kushner arrive in Moscow to meet with Putin, discuss Ukraine peace talksRussia's federal Investigative Committee said in a post to Telegram that it had opened a terrorism case into the incident, saying that Ukrainian attacks had caused "damage to the structure."

Russian Deputy Prime Minister Marat Khusnullin briefed Russian President Vladimir Putin on the latest developments regarding the bridge, Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov told reporters on Tuesday, according to the state-run Tass news agency.

Putin did not publicly comment on the latest strikes before departing for China, where he is expected to meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping and U.S. President Donald Trump this week. Peskov did not rule out that the attacks in Crimea were connected to the upcoming trilateral meeting.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirmed the attack in a post to social media, uploading a video that appeared to have been shot by a munition heading toward the bridge.

This grab taken from a video released on Nov. 17, 2026 on the official Telegram channel of Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy allegedly shows a missile flying toward the Crimean bridge that links Crimea to Russia, near Kerch.Handout/Telegram / @V_Zelensky_official/RelatedRussia, Ukraine and US meet for Abu Dhabi talks as Trump says war can 'end soon'Zelenskyy described the strike as an "unprecedented operation in response to Russian attacks on our infrastructure."

"This is the result of the seventh stage of an operation that has been underway for several weeks," Zelenskyy said, adding that past weeks have seen the systematic targeting of Russian defenses along the route to the bridge.

Ukraine used a mix of drones and missiles to strike the bridge, Zelenskyy said, including a "precision-guided strike" by an FP-5 Flamingo cruise missile.

"We have repeatedly offered Russia de-escalation steps, but we have only received loud rejections to all our proposals. Russia continues to strike our infrastructure every day, including bridges in Zaporizhzhia, Dnipro, Kyiv, and the Odesa region," the Ukrainian president wrote.

"Ukraine's defense potential is high and will remain so, and we will never leave unanswered the terror against our cities and people," he added.

This grab taken from a video released on Nov. 17, 2026 by the Ukrainian Security Service shows damage to the Crimean bridge that links Crimea to Russia, near Kerch.Handout/UKRAINIAN SECURITY SERVICE/AFP vRelatedUkraine fires 1,336 drones into Russia in one of war's largest attacks, Moscow saysA cruise missile produced by the Fire Point company was among those used to hit the bridge, a senior company official told ABC News. The company said in a post to Telegram that its drones and missiles inflicted "critical damage" on the bridge, with nearly 900 feet of road surface destroyed and the collapse of one of the bridge's two arches.

Ukraine's General Staff said of the attack in a statement posted to social media, "The roadway is out of action: no vehicle can cross it. The railway section is still standing, but now with a damaged arch."

The bridge connects Crimea to the southwestern Russian region of Krasnodar Krai. Construction began after Moscow seized Crimea from Ukraine in 2014, following the pro-Western Maidan Revolution in Kyiv and Russia's subsequent invasion of the peninsula and fomentation of separatist revolt in eastern Ukraine.

The bridge was personally opened by Putin, the flagship project standing as a prominent symbol of Russia's control of Crimea. Ukraine has repeatedly attacked the structure during Moscow's full-scale invasion, which began in 2022. The road-rail bridge is also a key supply route for the supply of Russian units, naval and air bases on the peninsula.

Russia's Defense Ministry said Ukraine launched 1,441 drones into the country overnight, which -- according to ministry statements analyzed by ABC News -- constituted one of the largest Ukrainian drone attacks of the war to date. From Sunday night through Monday, the ministry said Ukraine launched 1,484 drones into the country.

A satellite image shows a bridge over the Kerch Strait, Crimea, on Nov. 16, 2026.2026 Planet Labs Pbc/via ReutersRelatedUkraine must 'unblock' Patriot missile delivery, Zelenskyy says after deadly strikesThe ministry said drones were downed over 21 regions -- Moscow among them -- plus occupied Crimea, the Black Sea and the Sea of Azov.

Moscow Mayor Sergey Sobyanin said that 800 drones were launched toward Moscow, with most destroyed "at long range." Sobyanin said in posts to Telegram that 321 drones were downed on approach to the capital.

All four of Moscow's international airports were put under temporary flight restrictions during the overnight attacks, Rosaviatsiya -- Russia's federal air transport agency -- said in a series of statements posted to Telegram.

Airports in Kaluga, Penza, Saratov, Cherepovets, Samara, Ulyanovsk, Yaroslavl, Orenburg, Bugulma, Kazan, Nizhnekamsk, Cheboksary, Ufa and Tambov were also put under restrictions, Rosaviatsiya said.

Russia continued its long-range strike campaign against Ukraine overnight. Ukraine's air force said Russia launched 306 drones, 92 of which were jet-powered, and an unspecified number of ballistic and cruise missiles into the country in its latest attack.

The air force said defenders downed or suppressed three air-to-ground missiles, three cruise missiles and 205 drones, of which 48 were jet-powered. Impacts were recorded across 44 locations, the air force said.

Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said in posts to Telegram that Russian ballistic missiles targeted the capital's Northern and Southern bridges which span the Dnipro River.

Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko speaks from a bridge damaged in reported Russian attacks on Kyiv, Ukraine, on Nov. 17, 2026, in this screengrab taken from a video.Vitali Klitschko Via Telegram/via ReutersRelatedRussia-Ukraine talks end without breakthrough announcement amid barrage of dronesKlitschko said that traffic on both bridges was suspended while a damage assessment was being carried out.

At least two people were killed and another person was injured in the Russian strikes on Kyiv, according to the State Emergency Service of Ukraine.

Elsewhere in Ukraine, Russian strikes killed at least three people in Chernihiv, killed one person and wounded 31 others in Zaporizhzhia, killed one person and injured another in Vinnytsia, wounded six people in Smila and injured seven people in Dnipro, according to regional authorities.

Regional officials reported widespread power outages in the city of Dnipro and the wider Dnipropetrovsk region.

Local officials also reported Russian attacks in western Ukrainian regions including Lviv, Rivne, Ternopil and Chernivtsi. Across Ukraine's western border in Poland, the country's Operational Command said that "necessary air defense forces and assets" were activated in response to the Russian attacks.

Russia's Defense Ministry said its overnight attacks targeted military, transport and energy facilities in the Kyiv, Zaporizhzhia, Cherkasy, Dnipropetrovsk and Kharkiv regions, along with port infrastructure and cargo ships in the Odesa region.

ABC News' Oleksiy Pshemyskyi, Natalia Popova, Patrick Reevell, Tanya Stukalova and Morgan Winsor contributed to this report.

Ukraine targeted the Crimean bridge for a second consecutive night on Monday, according to Ukrainian officials and Russian-aligned authorities on the occupied Ukrainian peninsula, with Kyiv claiming to have inflicted serious damage on the structure.

Russia's federal Investigative Committee said in a post to Telegram that it had opened a terrorism case into the incident, saying that Ukrainian attacks had caused "damage to the structure."

Zelenskyy described the strike as an "unprecedented operation in response to Russian attacks on our infrastructure."

A cruise missile produced by the Fire Point company was among those used to hit the bridge, a senior company official told ABC News. The company said in a post to Telegram that its drones and missiles inflicted "critical damage" on the bridge, with nearly 900 feet of road surface destroyed and the collapse of one of the bridge's two arches.

The ministry said drones were downed over 21 regions -- Moscow among them -- plus occupied Crimea, the Black Sea and the Sea of Azov.

Klitschko said that traffic on both bridges was suspended while a damage assessment was being carried out.
